newsitem.title: CHILE: Chileans pore over smiling guerrilla pictures.
newsitem.headline: Chileans pore over smiling guerrilla pictures.

text.p: Chilean authorities said they were scrutinising pictures splashed across newspapers Wednesday of three smiling leftist guerrillas who escaped from jail in December by helicopter.
The pictures shocked Chileans both because they were the first public photographs of the rebels since their escape and because of their taunting grins.

"They are being analysed ... for information," said national police chief Fernando Cordero. A special prosecutor investigating the jailbreak said he too wanted to examine the photos and letters sent by the rebels to their parents.

But Cordero signalled police had no clue as to whether the Manuel Rodriguez Patriotic Front rebels, seen standing in front of a Chilean flag and the group's red-and-blue flag, were still in Chile or outside the country.
"I think it's possible they're still in Chile, but maybe they're not. They're not about to tell us," Cordero told reporters.
The mother of guerrilla Ricardo Palma said a stranger handed her the pictures of her son, Pablo Munoz and Patricio Ortiz. She then offered the pictures to news media.

The three men, who all appear to be in their 20s, were convicted of involvement in ransom kidnappings in the 1980s and the murder of rightist politician Jaime Guzman in 1991. They were among four rebels plucked from a top-security jail on Dec. 30, 1996 by a helicopter.
They looked tanned and relaxed, leading some local news media to suggest they might be in a beach resort.

The publication of the pictures infuriated members of rightist opposition parties, who have long accused President Eduardo Frei's government of dragging its feet in prosecuting the Guzman assassination.

"This is a failure for the government. First, a failure that these people were allowed to escape from jail, and a failure now to see the publication of these smiling faces," said deputy Andres Allamand, head of the centre-right National Renewal party.
